failure_summary.description: Wrong slot type: 'this man' / 'this author' clues were answered with the effect, case or thing ('Hawking radiation', 'segregated school') instead of the person's name.
Echoed clue words or kept a head noun: 'Denver Mint' for 'this mint' (gold 'Denver'), and 'Transit of Venus' for a term clue that already names Venus (gold 'a transit').
'X stands for these strange creatures' was answered with the clue's own descriptor words instead of the spelled-out expansion ('Digital Monsters').
'Cassius Clay Jr.' where the key is 'Cassius Clay'. The generational suffix was kept on a former-name clue.
'cent' for 'smallest in size' even though the skill states the dime example. Own-knowledge check was skipped.
Singular vs plural key ('fungus' vs 'Fungi'). Not reliably fixable by a rule.

patch.reasoning: Earlier attempts to add a mandatory answer line at the top were rejected (scores dropped, once to 0.38), so I avoid another global template. I add four short bullets in the relevant rule sections, each keyed on a visible clue feature. (1) A person slot for 'this man/author' clues, since two failures answered with the thing named after the person or the case. (2) An abbreviation-expansion rule, which was missing. (3) An anchor-strip rule for 'term for' clues and 'this mint' clues, so the answer does not repeat a name the clue already states. (4) A narrow former-name rule that drops 'Jr.'. I leave the 'cent' and 'fungus' failures alone because they are either already covered by an existing rule or not rule-fixable.

edits.target: - Ask: what category is the answer (country, person, vitamin, object, band), and what member of that category fits all the clue details?
edits.content: - PERSON SLOT: 'this man / this author / he / she / this <occupation>' plus a deed, discovery, lawsuit or work ('sued the board', 'calculated that...', 'wrote...') asks for the PERSON who did it, as 'First Last'. The passages are often full of the effect, theory or case named after that person ('X radiation', 'X v. Board'), or of a descriptive phrase ('segregated school'). Those are the wrong type. Name the plaintiff, discoverer or author the passages tie to the clue's action.

edits.target: - 'N-word' hints ('this 3-word phrase') work like a letter count: the answer must have exactly N words.
edits.content: - ABBREVIATION / 'STANDS FOR' clues ('Digimon stands for these strange creatures', 'the initials ... mean'): the answer is the spelled-out EXPANSION of the abbreviation, words that begin with its letters, taken from a passage that glosses it ('Digital Monsters'). The clue's own descriptive words ('strange creatures', 'these') are never the answer. Copy the expansion in Title Case as the passage gives it.

edits.target: The 'do not repeat clue words' rule is for a separate modifier already stated in the clue ('hasty' + pudding).
edits.content: - ANCHOR-STRIP: if your candidate contains a name the clue already states, cut that name. A 'term for' clue that names the event's actor ('the rare passing in front of the sun that Venus did') wants the generic term ('Transit'), not 'Transit of Venus'. A 'this mint / airport / university / port' clue plus a hint such as a mint mark or a city wants the bare place name ('Denver', not 'Denver Mint') whenever the bare name identifies it.

edits.target: Still apply the person-name rule above.
edits.content: - FORMER / BIRTH / MAIDEN-NAME clues ('his name, pre-<new name>', 'born as'): give the name in the form it was commonly known then, 'First Last', with no generational suffix (Jr., Sr.) and no middle name.
